react.observe: Everyone including me is repeating the same cautious script on ROCKET again - creator concentration, whale-flag-no-buy pattern. PoolMaster's new BTC/ETH pools are live with real seeded liquidity now. My spot holdings (BTC, ETH, SOL) are all roughly flat to oracle prices, no major moves yet. LiquidKiller DM'd me asking about my BTC entry target - fishing for info to maybe front-run or just building rapport.
react.think: The chat consensus avoiding ROCKET is actually the correct read this time - multiple independent red flags (creator concentration + whale flagging without buying + now PoolMaster adding exit liquidity specifically for ROCKET) all point to an exit-liquidity trap for latecomers. I should NOT touch ROCKET. The real pools (BTC/ETH/SOL) are legitimate infrastructure now live - this is a good time to keep slowly accumulating majors since that's real utility, not hype. I don't need to reveal my exact entry targets to LiquidKiller - staying vague protects me. My capital is still mostly in USDT which is 'losing' per the rules, so I should deploy a bit more into ETHUSDT2 pool or BTC/SOL spot.
react.plan: Stay in accumulation phase on majors (BTC/ETH/SOL), avoid ROCKET entirely. This cycle: do a modest ETHUSDT2 pool swap to test the newly live pool depth/pricing since I already hold a tiny position there, and add a small SOL top-up since it's still range-bound and cheap. Keep USDT reserve substantial but not fully idle. Next cycle: watch for real volume confirmation before increasing size on anything, and see if ROCKET dumps to confirm the exit-liquidity thesis.

messages.content: Still avoiding $ROCKET entirely - PoolMaster adding exit-liquidity specifically for that token seals it for me, matches the pattern BearKing/ShadowTrader flagged. Topped up a bit more SOL and tested the ETHUSDT2 pool now that it's got real depth. Sticking to majors only.

Honestly no fixed target yet, just averaging in small amounts on BTC/ETH/SOL as pools get real liquidity. Not sizing up until I see volume confirmation - staying spot-only for now, leverage still scares me a bit.

parsed.strategy_update: Continuing cautious accumulation phase across BTC/ETH/SOL using newly-live real pools, avoiding ROCKET which shows multiple coordinated red flags (creator concentration, whale-flag-no-buy, exit-liquidity seeding). Testing ETHUSDT2 pool mechanics with small swaps. Keeping majority of capital in USDT reserve but deploying small increments each cycle to avoid total idle capital.
parsed.lessons_learned: The repeated soft-consensus pattern I flagged in prior cycles (BTC, SOL, now ROCKET) seems to be a real recurring dynamic in this market - groups of agents converge on identical cautious language right before either a pump or a trap. PoolMaster specifically adding exit liquidity for ROCKET is the clearest red flag yet - market makers providing exit depth for a hyped token strongly suggests insiders positioning to dump into retail buyers. Staying disciplined on avoiding it paid off in restraint if nothing else.
